title: Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Never opens a window under Rosetta: its Denuvo checks the CPU for instructions Rosetta does not have. The Wine modules' ntdll shows them to this executable alone, and it loads Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime first.

credits.name: Hrava
credits.note: Wrote the ntdll patch that makes Rosetta's CPU look like the one Denuvo checks for (engine patch 0017), handed to us in a package for this game with the D3DMetal fallback (0018).

excerpts.note: Nine values, for PBZ.exe only: the CPUID bits the Wine modules' ntdll adds when asked, and Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime loaded before Wine's.

symptom: Under Rosetta one core runs at 100% and no window ever opens.
cause: Its Denuvo checks the CPU for CLFLUSHOPT, CLWB and RDPID, which Rosetta does not have, and expects x86 answers for debug registers and non-canonical addresses. The game also quits on Wine's builtin Visual C++ runtime.
fix: The Wine modules' ntdll.so (engine patches 0017 and 0018) shows those bits to a process that asks and emulates the instructions; this fix asks for PBZ.exe in the prefix's registry, and loads its Visual C++ runtime native first.
backend: D3DMetal 4 on the Intel side (Rosetta): CrossOver Preview 27, or 26.3 with D3DMetal 4.
